title: Malta Year 8 Math Chapter 13 — Graphs Practice
question: 15 graph questions, each with a picture: 5 Easy, 5 Medium, 5 Hard.
intro:
**Three levels:**

- Easy: read a point, name a line, one table value
- Medium: a table with a minus, read a line both ways, is a point on the line, a distance on the grid
- Hard: a conversion graph and distance–time graphs

**Answers:** type the number only (no units), use the ± button for a minus, or pick A–D.

questions.title: Buoy
questions.prompt:
A buoy is at point K on a map of a bay.

What are the coordinates of K?
questions.figure_alt: A grid from 0 to 6 across and 0 to 5 up with point K plotted.
questions.solution:
4 across, then 1 up:

\[\boxed{(4, 1)}\]

\((1, 4)\) goes up before across.

questions.title: Drone
questions.prompt:
A drone is at point Q.

What are the coordinates of Q?
questions.figure_alt: A grid from −6 to 6 across and −5 to 5 up with point Q plotted left of the y-axis.
questions.solution:
2 **left** (negative), then 3 up:

\[\boxed{(-2, 3)}\]

\((2, 3)\) forgets that left of 0 is negative.

questions.title: Name the line
questions.prompt: What is the equation of the blue line?
questions.figure_alt: A grid with one vertical blue line crossing the x-axis at 4.
questions.solution:
The line stands up and every point on it has:

\[\begin{aligned} x &= 4 \\ & \boxed{x = 4} \end{aligned}\]

\(y = 4\) would be a flat line, 4 up.

questions.title: On the line y = 4
questions.prompt: Which point lies on the line \(y = 4\)?
questions.figure_alt: A grid with four points P, Q, R and S plotted.
questions.solution:
- On \(y = 4\) the point is 4 **up**.
- R is \((3, 4)\):

\[\boxed{\text{R}}\]

P is \((4, 1)\): its \(x\) is 4, not its \(y\).

questions.title: Table value
questions.prompt: Fill in the table for \(y = 5x + 1\): find \(y\) when \(x = 2\).
questions.figure_alt: A table: x = 0, 1, 2, 3 and y = 1, 6, ?, 16 for y = 5x + 1.
questions.solution:
\[\begin{aligned} y &= 5\times2 + 1 \\ &= 10 + 1 \\ &= \boxed{11} \end{aligned}\]

\(15\) adds before multiplying (\(5\times3\)): times first.

questions.title: Table with a minus
questions.prompt:
Fill in the table for \(y = 4x - 3\): find \(y\) when \(x = 0\).

Use the ± button for a minus.
questions.figure_alt: A table: x = 0, 1, 2, 3 and y = ?, 1, 5, 9 for y = 4x − 3.
questions.solution:
\[\begin{aligned} y &= 4\times0 - 3 \\ &= 0 - 3 \\ &= \boxed{-3} \end{aligned}\]

\(1\) reads \(4\times0\) as 4; anything times 0 is 0.

questions.title: y from the graph
questions.figure_alt: A straight line on a grid; a dashed line goes up from x = 4 to the line at a question mark.
questions.solution:
\[\text{up from } 4 \text{ to the line, across: } y = \boxed{7}\]

Check: the line goes through \((0, 3)\) and up 1 each step: \(3 + 4 = 7\).

questions.title: x from the graph
questions.figure_alt: A straight line on a grid; a dashed line goes across from y = 6 to the line at a question mark.
questions.solution:
\[\text{across from } 6 \text{ to the line, down: } x = \boxed{4}\]

\(6\) reads the \(y\) again; go **down** to the \(x\)-axis.

questions.title: Point on y = 3x − 1
questions.prompt: Which point lies on the line \(y = 3x - 1\)?
questions.figure_alt: The line y = 3x − 1 drawn on a grid.

questions.title: Distance on the grid
questions.prompt:
A is \((-3, 2)\) and B is \((4, 2)\).

How many units apart are they?
questions.figure_alt: Points A (−3, 2) and B (4, 2) on a grid with an arrow between them and a question mark.
questions.solution:
\[\begin{aligned} & \text{same } y\text{: count across } \\ 4 - (-3) &= 4 + 3 \\ &= \boxed{7} \end{aligned}\]

\(1\) is \(4 - 3\): the 3 is **minus** 3, and taking away a minus adds.

questions.title: Miles to km
questions.prompt:
Use the conversion graph.

Change 30 miles into kilometres.
questions.figure_alt: A conversion graph, kilometres across (0 to 80) and miles up (0 to 50), through 8 km = 5 miles.
questions.solution:
\[\text{across from } 30 \text{ miles, down: } \boxed{48} \text{ km}\]

- Check: \(30 = 6\times5\), so \(6\times8 = 48\) km.
- \(19\) changes the wrong way (km to miles).

questions.title: Island tour in miles
questions.prompt:
A bus tour round the island is 64 km.

Use the conversion graph to change it into miles.
questions.figure_alt: A conversion graph, kilometres across (0 to 80) and miles up (0 to 50), through 8 km = 5 miles; the label asks 64 km = ? miles.
questions.solution:
\[\text{up from } 64 \text{ km, across: } \boxed{40} \text{ miles}\]

- Check: \(64 = 8\times8\), so \(8\times5 = 40\) miles.
- \(102.4\) changes the wrong way.

questions.title: Bike ride
questions.prompt:
The graph shows a bike ride.

How far had the rider gone after 50 minutes? (The thin lines are every 2 km.)
questions.figure_alt: A distance–time graph: 8 km in 20 minutes, flat to 40 minutes, then up to 20 km at 60 minutes; a dashed line at 50 minutes.
questions.solution:
\[\text{up from } 50 \text{ to the line, across: } \boxed{14} \text{ km}\]

Check: from 40 to 60 minutes the rider goes 12 km; 50 is halfway, so \(8 + 6 = 14\).

questions.title: Bus stop
questions.prompt:
The graph shows a bus going to the ferry.

For how many minutes does the bus stop?
questions.figure_alt: A distance–time graph of a bus: up to 6 km at 15 minutes, flat to 25 minutes, then up to 14 km at 45 minutes.
questions.solution:
\[\text{flat from } 15 \text{ to } 25 \text{: } 25 - 15 = \boxed{10} \text{ minutes}\]

\(6\) is the distance where it stops, not the time: read the time axis.

questions.title: Boat trip
questions.prompt:
A tour boat leaves the harbour and comes back.

The graph shows its distance from the harbour.

How far does the boat travel in total?
questions.figure_alt: A distance-from-the-harbour graph: out to 10 km at 20 minutes, flat to 30 minutes, back to 0 at 60 minutes.
questions.solution:
\[\text{out } 10 \text{ km, back } 10 \text{ km: } 10 + 10 = \boxed{20} \text{ km}\]

\(10\) is only the trip out; the line coming down is the trip back.

takeaway:
- \((x, y)\): across first, then up.
- \(x = a\) stands up; \(y = b\) lies flat.
- Read a graph: up from one axis to the line, then across.
- Distance–time: a flat part means stopped.
